paras: The killing of Daniel King was the fatal shooting of a drummer-boy at Kenner, Louisiana, on a Saturday evening in early October 1882, during the fall election season. The two surviving accounts disagree on who he was: a Mississippi weekly described a Black Democrat boy shot by a crowd of Black Republicans, while a wire brief called him a white drummer-boy killed in a political riot.
According to the Brookhaven Ledger, King was a Democrat who had agreed to drum for an "Ellis meeting" and had loaned his drum to some Black men.

When King asked for the drum back, the men refused, and when he tried to take it, "several of the crowd opened fire on and killed him," the Ledger reported. The wire version said only that a "serious riot" occurred at a political meeting at Kenner "the other night," that King was killed, and that several Black men were hurt.
The shooters fled and, as of the Ledger's report, were being pursued by the sheriff. No report of arrests, an inquest or a trial appears in the coverage.

The Brookhaven Ledger carried the earliest and fullest item on October 12, casting the episode in partisan terms as "a crowd of Republican negroes" killing a boy who "was a Democrat." A week later a one-sentence brief beginning "A SERIOUS riot" ran among unrelated crimes and accidents in weeklies in Arkansas, Tennessee and Kansas, and on October 21 in Louisiana's St. Landry Democrat and Mississippi's Panola Weekly Star. None of these papers commented on the killing, and the brief's description of King as white was repeated unchanged from paper to paper.

The accounts conflict on King's race, "a little negro boy" in the Ledger and "a white drummer-boy" in the wire, and on whether the killing was a riot or a shooting by one side's crowd. The Ledger's item appeared earlier and gave a specific day, a cause and the sheriff's pursuit, while the wire brief gave no source or detail.

reader.title: Killing of Daniel King at Kenner, Louisiana
bases: The fuller report (A1) describes a Black boy shot by a crowd of Black Republicans in a political quarrel over a drum, while the wire brief (A2) calls the victim white and the affair a riot with Black men hurt; neither describes white violence against Black people.

Two independent reports agree that a drummer named King was killed at a political gathering in Kenner (A1, A2), but they contradict each other on his race and on whether it was a riot or a shooting by a crowd of Black Republicans.

framing.detail: The Brookhaven Ledger gave a short local-news item casting the killers as 'Republican negroes' and the victim as a Democrat, with no editorial comment.
